note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The consensus EPS bar ($2.18, Autoliv consensus page 2026-10-19) sits about 5% below what the same consensus adj EBIT ($253m) converts to: Q3 2025 turned $271m adj EBIT into $2.32 adj EPS on ~77m shares, and shares outstanding fell from 73,237,217 (10 July 2026) to 72,006,695 (30 Sept 2026, 1,232,671 retired in Q3), so an in-line $253m EBIT maps to roughly $2.28-2.32 adj EPS; the EPS low of $1.83 suggests some estimates in the average are not on an adjusted basis.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells headline quarters: Q2 2026 (adj EPS $2.43, record Q2 sales, guide kept) -3.78; Q3 2025 (record Q3 sales, op income and EPS) -2.62; 5 of the last 7 reactions negative, the two positives both Q1 prints.

findings.finding: S&P Global Mobility puts Q3 2026 global light-vehicle production at -1.6% y/y (cited in Valeo's Q3 sales release, 2026-10-22), better than the ~-3% H2 run-rate implied by Autoliv's FY assumption of -2.5% after H1 (Q1 -3.4%, Q2 -0.3%); but the regional split derived from Valeo's table (North America ~-5%, China ~-6%, Europe ~0%, Asia ex-China ~+4.5%, South America ~+6%) hits the Americas, where Autoliv underperformed LVP by 4.9pp in Q2 (32% of sales), so applying Q2's regional outperformance gives organic roughly -0.5% to 0% and sales near, perhaps ~0.5% below, the $2,718m bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 organic +3.9% trailed LVP +4.6% and the stock fell -2.62; Q1 2026 organic +0.8% vs LVP -3.4% (4.2pp outperformance) bought +6.82; Q2 2026 outperformance ~1.3pp with Americas -4.9pp sold -3.78. Outperformance vs LVP is the line this name trades on at the top line.

findings.finding: Raw-material inflation from the Persian Gulf conflict did not ease in Q3 and Autoliv named helium (an airbag-inflator input) as the main driver: Autoliv's gross headwind estimate rose from ~$90m (Q1 call) to ~$110m (Q2), Nippon Sanso raised helium prices >30% from July 2026, and Hormuz commodity transits were 4 vessels on 15 Sept against ~125/day pre-war; the FY guide of 10.5-11% needs ~14-15% Q4 margin on customer compensations, so a trim toward or below the low end is the main downside on the print, against a consensus already at 10.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: guide kept but margin cadence pushed to Q4 and raw-material headwind raised to $110m, stock -3.78. Q4 2025 print (2026 first guide) -4.11. Guidance-cadence news has been sold on this name.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 6.76% of float / 6.2 days to cover at 30 Sept 2026 (up 7.3% on the prior record and from ~2.5% / 3.1 days a year earlier) while the Q3 EPS consensus was cut from ~$2.26 (July) to $2.18 (Oct 19), so the bar has been lowered and shorts have built for a guide disappointment; a held guide meets a short base that needs ~6 days of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline carried this level of short interest; the two up-reactions (Q1 2025 +5.56, Q1 2026 +6.82) both came on prints that cleared a lowered bar after a weak tape.

findings.finding: Valeo, reporting Q3 sales on 2026-10-22 in the same input-cost environment, confirmed its FY2026 guidance and said H2 operating margin and FCF will be at least H1 levels, with Q4 sequential growth in line with seasonality; a peer that holds a margin guide the day before is weak evidence that Gulf-driven cost inflation has not broken European supplier guides.

findings.finding: The consensus revenue bar ($3.35-3.40bn) implies only +2.6-4.1% sequential growth over Q2's $3.27bn. Q2 ended with record backlog of $14.06bn, +$1.61bn (+13%) q/q, and Q1 to Q2 revenue grew +14%. FIX has beaten revenue every quarter, including Q2 by 11% ($3.27bn against $2.94bn), so the arithmetic points to another revenue beat of a few percent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold in 2026: Q1 (2026-04-23) -2.69% and Q2 (2026-07-23) -5.33% on an 11% revenue beat with backlog +13% q/q. In 2025 the same line bought +22.4% (Jul) and +19.0% (Oct). The response has turned from strongly positive to negative as the multiple stretched.

findings.finding: Revenue from estimate changes on prior-period performance obligations (catch-ups) added 8.1% of revenue in Q1 2026 and 7.7% in Q2 2026, against 4.0% in Q3 2025, 4.4% in Q2 2025 and 1.7% in Q3 2024. About $230-250m a quarter of H1 revenue, at high incremental margin, came from favourable re-estimates. That puts the quality of the 25.9-26.3% gross margin at risk if Q3 catch-ups revert toward the 4% of a year ago, which would take roughly 2-4 points of revenue and some margin off the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior case of margin disappointing on FIX in the baseline. The last two prints, with gross margin at records (Q1 26.3%, Q2 25.9%), still fell -2.7% and -5.3%, so the market was already discounting margin quality.

findings.finding: The FY2026 same-store growth guide (mid-to-high 30%, set on the Q2 call) is below where consensus sits (+42.1% FY revenue). H1 same-store was +47%, so a raise or firming of the FY guide with a first 2027 read is the likely forward-looking content of this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 guide raise (to mid-to-high 30% from mid-to-high teens in February) came with -5.33%. The Feb 2026 initial guide of mid-to-high teens came with +6.46%.

findings.finding: Into the print, the stock fell from about $69.8bn market cap (10-05) to about $45bn at the sealed spot: -22% over 20 days, -13.6% over 5 days, and about -8.6% intraday on 10-22 alone ($1,401 on 10-21 to $1,280). There was no company-specific news; the only stock-specific item was Goldman's target cut to $1,875 from $2,159 on 10-20 for 'multiple compression' while keeping Buy. A derating of this size lowers the multiple bar that sold the last two beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the baseline, the large positive reactions (+22.4% Jul 2025, +19.0% Oct 2025) came when the stock had not run ahead of fundamentals. The 2026 negative reactions came near highs ($1,756 in July). Today's setup, 38% off the high, has no direct precedent in the eight prints.

findings.finding: The print lands into a tape that is selling AI-infrastructure beats. On 10-22 the S&P 500 was -1.37% and XLK about -3% on broad AI selling, and Nokia fell about 10% the same morning despite a data-center-driven beat ($5.79bn revenue against $5.07bn consensus, AI & Cloud +123%), on cash conversion. Vertiv had an 11-session record losing streak into 10-20. AI power names (GEV -11%, VRT -14%, BE -15%) fell in the week to 10-20 on rate and AI-financing fears.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FIX fell -5.33% on a large Q2 beat when the AI tape was still strong. Peers on 10-22 show the same 'beat and sell' response.

findings.finding: Dodge Momentum Index for September 2026 (released 10-07): commercial planning -1.3% m/m and -3.0% y/y, with data centers named as the drag ('slower planning momentum after a surge in late 2025'). August's index was down 0.4% on 'weaker data center planning' and was revised lower. Ex-data-centers, commercial planning was -14.9% y/y, so data centers are still growing y/y but decelerating. This is the bookings/backlog line for FIX's Q3 (58.7% of Q2 revenue was Technology).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog is the line FIX trades on. Backlog +13% q/q in Q2 still came with -5.33%; there is no record of a backlog decline in the baseline window.

findings.finding: GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik said data centers' share of Electrification orders would fall to 'probably more like 20%' in Q3 2026. This is a read from an adjacent supplier into the same customers, on a quarter that covers FIX's Q3 bookings period.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. FIX's backlog has been the stock's driver.

findings.finding: Census construction spending: private data-center construction reached a record $84.95bn SAAR in August 2026, +73% y/y, accelerating from +36% (May), +55% (Jun) and +65% (Jul). That is the work-in-place series that maps to FIX's revenue burn in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have been sold in 2026 (-2.7%, -5.3%), so a confirmed strong burn has been worth little on the day.

findings.finding: Billings in excess of costs plus deferred revenue jumped $1.11bn in H1 2026, to $3.23bn from $2.12bn, which drove the $1.14bn Q2 operating cash flow. CFO Bill George attributed it to advance customer cash and said cash flow should align with net income plus non-cash items over time. A Q3 OCF that reverses toward earnings is the likely outcome, and a cash-conversion headline is what sank Nokia on 10-22.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's record cash flow came with -5.33%, so the market did not pay for the cash. It may not punish a reversal either.
